panel.access.pulses_only: the panel sends pulses, it does not know the state
panel.agenda.hidden_until: the section stays hidden until one appears
panel.agenda.no_calendar_entity: Home Assistant has no calendar entity
panel.boot.read_only_note: If something does not respond, the panel starts anyway in read-only mode.
panel.climate.floor_off_conflict: zones are calling for heat, but this floor is off
panel.climate.timer_no_effect: nothing will happen when it runs out: the automation is disabled
panel.common.section_not_ready: this section is not available yet
panel.diag.log_needs_network: The network is needed: the log is read from /api/log, and without an address there is nothing to scan.
panel.energy.curve_coming: today's curve is on its way…
panel.energy.no_statistics: the recorder has no statistics for this sensor
panel.home.openings_down: the openings sensor is not responding
panel.home.presence_down: the presence sensor is not responding
panel.robot.no_alerts_configured: No alerts configured. Add them from the configuration page, Robot section.
panel.robot.no_rooms: No rooms configured. Rooms are added from the configuration page: each one needs the number the robot gave it and the name you want to see here.
panel.robot.subtitle: room-by-room cleaning
panel.schedules.none: No groups: they are added from the configuration page.
panel.schedules.outside_hours: outside these hours motion does not switch on
panel.schedules.title: Schedules
panel.settings.always_open: always open from the configuration — it does not close
panel.settings.factory_reset_explain: erases configuration, Wi-Fi password and token
panel.settings.name_story: Foyer Panel takes its name from the foyer, the entrance of a house: where this panel is, and the point from which one enters the house and its systems. The word once meant the hearth too, the centre of the house.
panel.settings.opens_for_15: opens the web page for 15 minutes, then it closes by itself
panel.settings.plain: in the clear: the network is local
panel.settings.reconnect_explain: without waiting for the next attempt
panel.settings.reset_explain: The configuration, the Wi-Fi password and the Home Assistant token are erased. After the restart the panel starts again from the first setup, and putting it back on the network needs someone standing here.
panel.settings.rest_of_config: The rest of the configuration is done from http://%s.local, after unlocking it here.
panel.settings.restart_explain: the configuration and the credentials stay
panel.settings.revision_hint: finds the exact code running here
panel.settings.tagline: the home panel for Home Assistant
panel.settings.tls: over TLS, with the certificate checked
panel.setup.save_failed: I could not save: the panel's memory is not responding. Try again; if it keeps failing, the console is needed.
panel.setup.searching_explain: The radio is searching. If nothing shows up, the panel is too far from the router or the network is hidden: in that case the name is typed from the console.
panel.setup.title: Connect the panel
panel.setup.token_paste_tip: The token is long: better to paste it from http://%s.local, now that the network is up.
panel.setup.token_refused: Home Assistant does not accept it: create another one
panel.state.wifi_down_note: The panel keeps retrying by itself. If the router's password changed, or the network has another name, choose it here.
panel.switches.none: No switches configured. They are added from the configuration page: each needs the entity to control, a name and, if you like, an icon and the sensor of its power draw.
panel.switches.title: Switches
panel.wifi.no_networks: no networks to share: they are set up from the web page

web.broken.empty_hint: Sets that branch back to empty, so it can be filled in again here. The value it has now is lost, and nothing changes on the panel until you press “Save and apply”.
web.broken.rest: The rest of the page works: what you see above and below saves as usual.
web.broken.subtitle: not drawn
web.broken.text: This part could not be drawn: {error}.

contrast.bad.one: {n} pair is below the readability threshold. The panel will use it anyway — this is a warning, not a ban — but from a metre and a half it may not be readable.
contrast.bad.other: {n} pairs are below the readability threshold. The panel will use them anyway — this is a warning, not a ban — but from a metre and a half they may not be readable.

web.contrast.good: Every pair is above the readability threshold.
web.contrast.subtitle: readable from a metre and a half?
web.contrast.title: Contrast and preview

web.field.access.icon.label: Icon
web.field.access.id.label: Id
web.field.access.label: Gates and doors
web.field.access.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.access.pulse_ms.label: Pulse length (milliseconds)
web.field.access.state_sensor.label: State sensor (optional)
web.field.access.type.label: Type
web.field.appearance.accent.hint: The active section in the rail, the buttons, what is being touched. It gives the panel its character, and selection, busy button and reconnection band follow from it.
web.field.appearance.accent.label: Accent (active section, buttons)
web.field.appearance.background.hint: The ground under everything. On a wall panel at night it is best very dark: it is the largest surface, and the one that lights up the hallway.
web.field.appearance.background.label: Background
web.field.appearance.borders.hint: The one-pixel line around the tiles and under the headers.
web.field.appearance.borders.label: Borders
web.field.appearance.cards.hint: The tiles on top of the background — zones, lights, rows. It should stand out from the background only a little: too much, and the screen becomes a list of rectangles instead of a whole.
web.field.appearance.cards.label: Cards and tiles
web.field.appearance.hint: Nine are chosen here; all the others are derived from these. A missing colour is the default, the one the panel was designed with: deleting the block puts everything back as it was.
web.field.appearance.label: Interface colours
web.field.appearance.lights_on.hint: The bulb of a light that is on, in the Lights section, and its brightness bar. It has a colour of its own and does not follow the accent, because it is not a state of the interface: it is something lit in the house, and nobody looking at a green chandelier thinks of the panel's theme.
web.field.appearance.lights_on.label: Lights on (bulb and brightness)
web.field.appearance.negative.hint: Command failed, alarm, consumption. The backgrounds and texts of negative boxes follow from it.
web.field.appearance.negative.label: Negative (failed, alarms)
web.field.appearance.positive.hint: Command done, good news, battery charging. The backgrounds and texts of positive boxes follow from it.
web.field.appearance.positive.label: Positive (done, good news)
web.field.appearance.text.hint: The main text, and the icons that matter. Its pair with the background decides whether the panel reads from a metre and a half.
web.field.appearance.text.label: Main text
web.field.appearance.text_dim.hint: Subtitles, units, labels. It should read, not draw the eye: below a certain contrast, though, it simply stops reading.
web.field.appearance.text_dim.label: Secondary text
web.field.appliances.cycle.hint: The entity that says whether a cycle is running. On: it is working.
web.field.appliances.cycle.label: Running-cycle entity
web.field.appliances.hint: The appliances the home screen shows as running or not: two, side by side in a single card. The order here is the order on the screen.
web.field.appliances.label: Washer and dryer
web.field.appliances.max_power.hint: Watts at full load, for the bar under the name. Without it the bar is not drawn: a bar that does not know what it fills up against would lie.
web.field.appliances.max_power.label: Watts at full load
web.field.appliances.name.hint: How it appears on the panel. Short: the card is split in two, and «Tumble dryer» is already at the limit.
web.field.appliances.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.appliances.power.hint: The power sensor. Optional: without it, you only see whether it is working.
web.field.appliances.power.label: Power sensor
web.field.calendar.calendars.color.label: Colour
web.field.calendar.calendars.id.label: Calendar
web.field.calendar.calendars.label: Calendars
web.field.calendar.calendars.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.calendar.days.label: Days shown
web.field.calendar.enabled.label: Show the calendar
web.field.calendar.home_max_events.label: Events on the home screen
web.field.calendar.label: Calendar
web.field.calendar.sensor.label: Events sensor
web.field.climate.ac_limits.label: Air conditioner setpoint
web.field.climate.ac_limits.max.label: Maximum (°)
web.field.climate.ac_limits.min.label: Minimum (°)
web.field.climate.ac_limits.step.label: Step (°)
web.field.climate.air_conditioners.id.label: Id
web.field.climate.air_conditioners.label: Air conditioners
web.field.climate.air_conditioners.timer.hin: The «turn off with the timer» switch appears only when both this and «Timer automation» are filled in.
web.field.climate.floors.hint: The floors of the heating system. The valves of each zone open the circuit; the real switch-on is a switch per floor, and that is what goes here. Without floors the Heating section stays as it was: a single list, with no switches.
web.field.climate.floors.id.hint: How the zones call it. Lowercase letters, digits and underscore only.
web.field.climate.floors.id.label: Floor id (used by the zones)
web.field.climate.floors.label: Heating floors
web.field.climate.floors.name.hint: How it appears on the panel: «Floor 1», «Garage».
web.field.climate.floors.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.climate.floors.switch.hint: What turns on the heating of this floor. The command follows the domain, as for switches.
web.field.climate.floors.switch.label: Switch that turns the floor on
web.field.climate.heating.climate.label: Thermostat
web.field.climate.heating.floor.hint: The floor this zone belongs to. Zones without a floor do not disappear: they end up in a group of their own, because a zone you stop seeing is worse than a zone in the wrong group.
web.field.climate.heating.floor.label: Floor of this zone
web.field.climate.heating.humidity.label: Humidity sensor (optional)
web.field.climate.heating.label: Heating zones
web.field.climate.heating.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.climate.heating.temperature.label: Temperature sensor (optional)
web.field.climate.heating_limits.label: Heating setpoint
web.field.climate.heating_limits.max.label: Maximum (°)
web.field.climate.heating_limits.min.label: Minimum (°)
web.field.climate.heating_limits.step.label: Step (°)
web.field.climate.label: Climate
web.field.climate.panel_floor.hint: The floor THIS panel controls. The heating icon in standby and in the header follows from it: a panel is the thermostat of its floor, and tells the state of what it commands. Without it those two icons do not appear.
web.field.climate.panel_floor.label: Floor this panel controls
web.field.diagnostics.config_always_open.hin: Installation only. Keeps the configuration page always open, without the fifteen-minute window and without touching the glass. Turn it off when the panel is in place: while it is on, anyone on the home network can change the configuration and install a firmware.
web.field.diagnostics.label: Diagnostics
web.field.diagnostics.status_endpoint.label: Paths /api/status and /api/log
web.field.display.brightness_active.label: Brightness in use (%)
web.field.display.brightness_standby.label: Brightness in standby (%)
web.field.display.label: Screen
web.field.display.long_press_ms.label: Long press (milliseconds)
web.field.display.night_off.enabled.label: Turn the screen off at night
web.field.display.night_off.from.label: Turns off at
web.field.display.night_off.label: Night switch-off
web.field.display.night_off.to.label: Turns back on at
web.field.display.off_after_s.label: Seconds before the screen turns off (0: never)
web.field.display.off_when_nobody_home.hint: Turns the screen off when presence is known and nobody is home. A touch turns it back on; someone arriving turns it back on to standby.
web.field.display.off_when_nobody_home.label: Turn the screen off when nobody is home
web.field.display.return_home_after_s.label: Seconds before going back to home
web.field.display.standby.clock.hint: The time. 4 is the size the panel always had.
web.field.display.standby.clock.label: Size of the time (1-5)
web.field.display.standby.hint: How big the two lines of the standby screen are, from 1 (smallest) to 5 (largest). Five steps and not a free number: the fonts are images generated when the firmware is built, and a size never generated does not exist on the panel.
web.field.display.standby.label: Standby screen
web.field.display.standby.temperature.hint: The temperature under the time. 2 is the usual size.
web.field.display.standby.temperature.label: Size of the temperature (1-5)
web.field.display.standby_after_s.label: Seconds of inactivity before standby
web.field.energy.aggregate_sensor.label: Aggregate sensor
web.field.energy.attributes.battery_w.hint: Battery power. Positive or negative according to «Signs».
web.field.energy.attributes.battery_w.label: Battery power
web.field.energy.attributes.grid_w.hint: Power from the grid. Positive or negative according to «Signs».
web.field.energy.attributes.grid_w.label: Grid power
web.field.energy.attributes.hint: What the values the panel shows are called inside the aggregate sensor. The names were chosen by whoever wrote the template in Home Assistant.
web.field.energy.attributes.house_w.hint: House consumption. Without it, it is computed: production minus what goes to the grid and to the battery.
web.field.energy.attributes.house_w.label: House consumption
web.field.energy.attributes.label: Attributes of the aggregate sensor
web.field.energy.attributes.today_kwh.label: Produced today
web.field.energy.devices.entity.hint: The power sensor. Home Assistant declares the unit and the panel reads it: W or kW both work.
web.field.energy.devices.entity.label: Power sensor
web.field.energy.devices.hint: The sockets and appliances whose consumption you have. The panel sorts them from the hungriest down and draws as many as fit: the others are reached by scrolling the list.
web.field.energy.devices.label: Monitored devices
web.field.energy.devices.name.hint: What you call it at home: «Oven», not «sensor.oven_power».
web.field.energy.devices.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.energy.history.hint: The sensor the day's curve comes from. Empty: the aggregate sensor. It must have a state_class in Home Assistant, or the recorder keeps no hourly statistics and the curve stays empty — the panel says so instead of drawing a flat line.
web.field.energy.history.label: Daily curve sensor
web.field.energy.label: Energy
web.field.energy.signs.grid_positive.label: Positive grid power means
web.field.energy.signs.label: Signs
web.field.energy.strings.current.label: Current sensor
web.field.energy.strings.label: Photovoltaic strings
web.field.energy.strings.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.energy.strings.power.hint: Without it, the panel computes V × I and marks it as estimated.
web.field.energy.strings.power.label: Power sensor (optional)
web.field.energy.strings.voltage.label: Voltage sensor
web.field.energy.today.consumed.label: Consumed today
web.field.energy.today.exported.label: Fed into the grid today
web.field.energy.today.hint: The four totals at the bottom of the screen. They are energy (kWh), not power, and answer a different question from the numbers at the top: not «how much now» but «how much today». All optional.
web.field.energy.today.imported.label: Taken from the grid today
web.field.energy.today.label: Today's totals
web.field.energy.today.produced.hint: Produced by the photovoltaic system today.
web.field.energy.today.produced.label: Produced today
web.field.home.appliances.hint: Shows on the home screen whether the washer and the dryer are running. The block disappears by itself when they are not configured or Home Assistant does not answer.
web.field.home.appliances.label: Show washer and dryer
web.field.home.indoor_temperature.hint: Shows the room temperature in the header, next to the outdoor one. The sensor is the standby one — chosen once, in «Standby» — because two places saying which is the house thermometer could say two different things on the same glass.
web.field.home.indoor_temperature.label: Room temperature in the header
web.field.home.label: Home screen
web.field.home.robot.hint: Shows a robot row on the home screen: what it is doing and how much battery it has. Tapping it opens its section.
web.field.home.robot.label: Robot row on the home screen
web.field.home_assistant.host.hint: IP or host name, without scheme or path
web.field.home_assistant.host.label: Address
web.field.home_assistant.label: Home Assistant
web.field.home_assistant.port.label: Port
web.field.home_assistant.retry_s.label: Seconds between reconnection attempts
web.field.home_assistant.tls.label: Use HTTPS
web.field.home_assistant.ws_path.label: WebSocket path
web.field.house_state.label: House state
web.field.house_state.openings_sensor.label: Openings sensor
web.field.lights.label: Lights
web.field.lights.scenes.entity.label: Scene
web.field.lights.scenes.label: Scenes
web.field.lights.scenes.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.lights.zones.dimmable.label: Dimmable
web.field.lights.zones.entity.hint: The light. It can be a `switch.` instead of a `light.`: it happens with relays and some integrations, and the panel calls the right domain's service by itself. A `switch.` cannot be dimmed, though, so «dimmable» has no effect on it.
web.field.lights.zones.entity.label: Light
web.field.lights.zones.label: Zones
web.field.lights.zones.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.presence.label: Presence
web.field.presence.sensor.label: People sensor
web.field.robot.alerts.entity.hint: A two-state sensor, or an error sensor. The difference matters: a `sensor.` carries the message in its own state — «The clean-water Hall sensor was triggered…» — and then the panel shows that, as the robot wrote it, without rewriting it.
web.field.robot.alerts.entity.label: Sensor
web.field.robot.alerts.hint: What the robot's app reports: tanks, mop, filters, errors. An alert that is off appears nowhere; when at least one is on, a triangle appears next to the robot's name — on the home screen and in the section header — and opens this view.
web.field.robot.alerts.label: Alerts
web.field.robot.alerts.text.hint: The sentence to show. Needed for two-state sensors, because «on» is not a sentence; without it, the entity's name. Not needed for an error sensor: the robot's message wins.
web.field.robot.alerts.text.label: Sentence to show
web.field.robot.alerts.when.hint: Which of the two states is the alarm. It cannot be guessed, and getting it wrong says the opposite: «dirty water» on means empty it, but «mop attached» off means there is no mop.
web.field.robot.alerts.when.label: The alarm is when the sensor is
web.field.robot.battery.hint: The charge percentage sensor, for example sensor.robot_battery. Needed on recent integrations, where the battery is no longer an attribute of the robot. Left empty, the panel tries the battery_level attribute.
web.field.robot.battery.label: Battery sensor
web.field.robot.entity.hint: The robot's vacuum entity, for example vacuum.robot. State, battery and errors come from it, and the commands go to it.
web.field.robot.entity.label: Robot entity
web.field.robot.label: Robot vacuum
web.field.robot.maintenance.entity.hint: The time-left sensor. Home Assistant declares the unit, and it is not the same for everyone: the panel reads it and always shows hours.
web.field.robot.maintenance.entity.label: Time-left sensor
web.field.robot.maintenance.hint: The consumables: brushes, filter, sensors. Value and unit come from Home Assistant — the panel does not know how many hours a brush lasts, and must not.
web.field.robot.maintenance.label: Maintenance
web.field.robot.maintenance.name.hint: How it appears in the view. Without it, the name Home Assistant gives it.
web.field.robot.maintenance.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.robot.maintenance.threshold.hint: Below this value the item becomes an alert and makes the triangle appear. In hours, whatever unit the sensor uses: the panel turns seconds and minutes into hours before comparing, so a ten written here means ten hours for everyone. On sensors that are not a time — a percentage — their own unit applies. Without it, the item is only shown.
web.field.robot.maintenance.threshold.label: Warn when it drops below
web.field.robot.name.hint: What you call it at home. It appears in the row on the home screen and in the header of its section. Empty: «Robot».
web.field.robot.name.label: What it is called
web.field.robot.no_selection.hint: What the main command does when you have not chosen any room.
web.field.robot.no_selection.label: If you chose no rooms
web.field.robot.repeats.hint: How many times to go over each room. Only with the «Segments» form.
web.field.robot.repeats.label: Passes per room
web.field.robot.rooms.col.label: Column (1-6)
web.field.robot.rooms.height.label: Height in rows
web.field.robot.rooms.label: Rooms
web.field.robot.rooms.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.robot.rooms.number.hint: The number of the segment, which is not the one the app shows on the map: those are the order in which it lists them. The real numbers are read by calling the roborock.get_maps service from Developer tools, and on Roborock they start at 16.
web.field.robot.rooms.number.label: Number in the robot's map
web.field.robot.rooms.row.label: Row (1-4)
web.field.robot.rooms.width.label: Width in columns
web.field.robot.rooms_command.hint: The command the robot understands for cleaning single rooms. On Roborock it is app_segment_clean, and it is the only one needed: the robot's other commands — back to base, start, stop — the panel sends with Home Assistant's standard services, and they do not pass through here.
web.field.robot.rooms_command.label: Command for single rooms
web.field.robot.rooms_format.hint: How the room numbers are packed. «Segments» sends [{"segments":[20],"repeat":1}], the form of the native Roborock integration: measured on the real robot, it waits about fifty seconds and then really starts. «List» sends [20], the form of the old Xiaomi Miio: the robot accepts it, leaves the base, cleans fifteen seconds and goes back. If the robot does that, this is the first field to look at — and give the command a good minute before deciding it did not work.
web.field.robot.rooms_format.label: How the room numbers are sent
web.field.schedules.automations.entity.label: Automation
web.field.schedules.automations.hint: they appear on the panel in this order
web.field.schedules.automations.label: Automations
web.field.schedules.automations.name.hint: Optional: without it, the name the automation has in Home Assistant. For where the real one does not fit on a line.
web.field.schedules.automations.name.label: Name on the panel (optional)
web.field.schedules.entity.hint: The device the times switch on. Optional: a group can have only a validity window, with nothing to command.
web.field.schedules.entity.label: Commanded entity
web.field.schedules.hint: The things that run on a timetable: one group each, with the device it commands, the switch-on windows and the automations that fire them. The times live in Home Assistant's input_datetime — the panel reads and writes them, and keeps no copy.
web.field.schedules.icon.hint: The same closed list as the switches: it is the same question, and the icon glyphs are built into the firmware — a name outside the list would be an empty rectangle on the glass.
web.field.schedules.icon.label: Icon
web.field.schedules.label: Schedules
web.field.schedules.name.hint: How it appears at the top of the group, on the panel.
web.field.schedules.name.label: Group name
web.field.schedules.power.hint: The power sensor, if there is one.
web.field.schedules.power.label: Power sensor
web.field.schedules.windows.hint: when it turns on and when it turns off
web.field.schedules.windows.label: Windows
web.field.schedules.windows.off_time.label: Switch-off
web.field.schedules.windows.on_time.label: Switch-on
web.field.schedules.windows.validity.hint: Not a switch-on time but the interval in which another automation is allowed to fire — the corridor's motion light, say. It changes what the panel writes next to the times.
web.field.schedules.windows.validity.label: Validity window
web.field.schema.hint: The version of this file's layout. If it is newer than the firmware knows, the panel starts read-only.
web.field.schema.label: Schema version
web.field.sections.hint: The order is the one of the list above: it commands the rail and, on the home screen, the dock. The arrows change it. An unticked section appears in neither; one without its data source does not appear anyway.
web.field.sections.label: Sections
web.field.standby.climate.hint: Where «set 21.0°» and «heating» come from. Without it the two pills do not appear and the measured temperature remains.
web.field.standby.climate.label: Thermostat
web.field.standby.indoor_temperature.attribu: If set, this attribute of the entity is read instead of its state. For sensors that keep the value in an attribute.
web.field.standby.indoor_temperature.hint: The temperature of the room where the panel hangs. Without it the big number does not appear and standby shows the time alone.
web.field.standby.indoor_temperature.label: Room temperature
web.field.standby.indoor_temperature.label.h: What the room is called under the number: «in the living room». Without it, «at home».
web.field.standby.label: Standby
web.field.switches.entity.hint: What is turned on. The command follows the domain — switch.turn_on, light.turn_on, input_boolean.turn_on — and is not configured: write the entity and that is all.
web.field.switches.entity.label: Entity to turn on and off
web.field.switches.hint: Switches, sockets and smart lights that belong to no other list. The order here is the order on the screen; twelve fit on a page, beyond that it pages.
web.field.switches.icon.hint: The row's icon, among those built into the firmware. Without it, a socket. The list is closed because a name outside it would be an empty rectangle on the glass.
web.field.switches.icon.label: Row icon
web.field.switches.label: Switches
web.field.switches.name.hint: How it appears on the panel. Twenty-four characters: beyond that the row is cut with an ellipsis instead of squeezing the switch.
web.field.switches.name.label: Name on the panel
web.field.switches.power.hint: The power sensor, if this switch has one. It appears to the left of the switch. Without it the row leaves no empty space: it closes up.
web.field.switches.power.label: Power sensor
web.field.system.label: System
web.field.system.language.hint: The language of the panel and of this page. Without it, English. Any text can be changed in «Translations».
web.field.system.language.label: Language
web.field.system.network.hidden.label: Hidden network
web.field.system.network.label: Wi-Fi network
web.field.system.network.ssid.label: Network name (SSID)
web.field.system.ntp.label: Time servers (NTP)
web.field.system.panel_name.label: Panel name
web.field.system.profile.label: Screen profile
web.field.system.timezone.label: Time zone
web.field.weather.entity.label: Weather entity
web.field.weather.label: Weather
web.field.weather.local_temperature_attribut: If set, this attribute of the local sensor is read instead of its state. Without a local sensor it does nothing.
web.field.weather.local_temperature_sensor.h: The outdoor temperature sensor. It applies to the whole panel — the home header, standby and the «Outside» pill of the Climate section — and wins over the weather entity's temperature. Without it, the weather service's; without that either, «—».

web.section.access.lead: A pulse access sends a command and that is all: the panel does not know whether the gate opened, and indeed does not say so. Only one with a state sensor can show it.
web.section.access.title: Access
web.section.appearance.lead: Nine colours, and everything else follows. The backgrounds and texts of the states — selection, busy button, done, failed, alerts — are not chosen one by one: they are derived from these by rotating the hue, so they stay consistent whatever accent you choose. The values below are the ones the panel is drawn with now: change one and only that one changes. Contrast is computed and shown, not enforced — the panel obeys; and this page does not change colour, so from here you can always go back.
web.section.appearance.title: Colours
web.section.appliances.lead: The two appliances the home screen shows in a card split in half. The state comes from the cycle entity and not from the watts: a washer soaking draws as much as one that is off, and guessing the cycle from the power would mean announcing «done» halfway through the wash. The order here is the order on the screen, and decides the icon too: the first is the washer, the second the dryer.
web.section.appliances.title: Washer and dryer
web.section.calendar.lead: Without calendars the section does not appear on the panel: it is not a fault, it is the rule for a section without its data source.
web.section.calendar.title: Calendar
web.section.climate.lead: Two separate systems with different scales: the heating zones have only the setpoint, the air conditioners have mode, fan, louvre and timer.
web.section.climate.title: Climate
web.section.diagnostics.lead: The log on board and the two read-only paths. Turning status_endpoint off leaves no network surface exposed: the log on the panel stays.
web.section.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
web.section.energy.lead: The panel shows the values as Home Assistant gives them. The signs say which way the current flows: changing them here does not change the measurement, it changes how it reads.
web.section.energy.title: Energy
web.section.home.lead: Presence, openings, weather: what the home screen sums up at the top. The outdoor temperature sensor is here too, and applies to the home screen and to standby: when set, it wins over the weather service's — a sensor on the balcony knows the weather here, the service knows the weather in town.
web.section.home.title: Home
web.section.home_assistant.lead: The panel connects over WebSocket and listens for updates: it does not poll. The token is never returned by the page, it can only be replaced.
web.section.home_assistant.title: Home Assistant
web.section.lights.lead: One row per zone. The panel lays them out in grids, in the order chosen here: the first row is the first card of the first page.
web.section.lights.title: Lights
web.section.network.lead: How the panel sits on the home network. The Wi-Fi password is not in the configuration: it is a secret, written further down this page and never read back.
web.section.network.title: Network
web.section.robot.lead: The robot calls the rooms by the numbers it gave itself when it drew the map — 16, 17, 18 — and those numbers are read from its app. The name and position only you know: the position lays the rooms out on the panel as they are in the house, on a grid of six columns by four rows, so the kitchen is tapped because it is top right and not because it says so. Alerts and maintenance are the same things its app tells you: an error sensor brings the message already written and the panel shows that, while a two-state sensor wants a sentence of yours — and above all wants to know which of the two states is the alarm, because «mop attached» raises the alarm when it is off.
web.section.robot.title: Robot
web.section.schedules.lead: A group for each thing that runs on a timetable. The times are not here: they live in Home Assistant's input_datetime, and the panel reads and writes them — so they stay the same you see in your dashboard, and changing them in one place changes them in the other. The automations listed here can be turned off from the glass: it is how to pause a schedule without losing its times.
web.section.schedules.title: Schedules
web.section.screen.lead: Brightness and timings. These are the only settings that take effect at once, without restarting or reconnecting.
web.section.screen.title: Screen
web.section.standby.lead: The screen the panel shows when nobody touches it — that is, almost all the time it is on. The panel stands in for a thermostat, so the room temperature is as big as the time. The outdoor temperature is set in «Home», together with the weather.
web.section.standby.title: Standby
web.section.status.lead: What the panel says about itself. These are the same two paths that answer even when the configuration is closed.
web.section.status.title: Status and log
web.section.switches.lead: Sockets, smart lights, heaters, pumps: what turns on and off and nothing more, and belongs to no other list. The command follows the entity's domain — switch, light, input_boolean — and is not configured: write the entity and that is all. The icon is chosen from a closed list because the icon glyphs are built into the firmware, and a name outside the list would be an empty rectangle on the glass. The power sensor is optional: when there is one, the number appears to the left of the switch; when there is none, the row leaves no empty space.
web.section.switches.title: Switches
web.section.translations.lead: Every text of the panel and of this page, in every language the firmware carries. What you save here stays on the panel and takes the place of the built-in text; take it back to the built-in one and firmware updates reach it again. «Export file» gives the whole language as i18n/<code>.json, ready to go into the project. The checks are the ones the firmware build runs: the same placeholders as English — %d and %s on the panel, {name} on this page — and on the panel only characters its fonts can draw.
web.section.translations.title: Translations
web.section.wifi.lead: The networks — up to five — the panel shows with a QR code. None is special: the first is only the first in the list. The passwords are secrets: they are written below and never read back, and row n uses password number n.
web.section.wifi.title: Wi-Fi sharing
